reason: The narrative centers on Moses as a leader confronted with the Israelites' ingratitude and contention. The people quarrel with Moses (וַיָּרֶב הָעָם עִם־מֹשֶׁה), demand water, and then accuse him of deliberately bringing them to the wilderness to perish (לָמָּה זֶּה הֶעֱלִיתָנוּ מִמִּצְרַיִם לְהָמִית אֹתִי) despite their recent deliverance from Egypt. Moses expresses desperation about their hostility (עוֹד מְעַט וּסְקָלֻנִי - 'a little more and they will stone me'). The place names explicitly commemorate this dynamic: Massah (מַסָּה - testing) and Meribah (מְרִיבָה - contention), labeled specifically for the people's contending and testing of God through their accusations against their leader.
